chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Concerning a Christian who killed a Muslim, then when he was seized he accepted Islam, he said: “Kill him for him.” It was said: “Then if he does not accept Islam?” He said: “He is handed over to the heirs of the slain; if they wish, they may kill, and if they wish, they may pardon, and if they wish, they may enslave him.” And if he had tangible property with him, he said: “He and his property are handed over to the heirs of the slain.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the murdered person who hold the claim
key_terms.أُقْتُلْهُ بِهِ: execute him in retaliation for the slain person
key_terms.عَيْنُ مَالٍ: identifiable tangible property belonging to the offender
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: the Muslim victim whose killing is the subject of retaliation
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٍّ: a Christian offender subject to the ruling discussed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a Christian who kills a Muslim and then accepts Islam after being captured?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding a Christian who kills a Muslim and then is apprehended. It distinguishes between the case where he accepts Islam after capture and where he does not, and it outlines the authority of the slain person's heirs regarding retaliation, pardon, or enslavement, as well as disposition of the offender's property.
